  "an2.1:2.2": "What two? ",

  "an2.1:2.4": "What is the fault apparent in the present life? ",
  "an2.1:2.5": "It’s when someone sees that kings have arrested a bandit, a criminal, and subjected them to various punishments—",
  "an2.1:2.6": "whipping, caning, and clubbing; cutting off hands or feet, or both; cutting off ears or nose, or both; the ‘porridge pot’, the ‘shell-shave’, the ‘Rāhu’s mouth’, the ‘garland of fire’, the ‘burning hand’, the ‘bulrush twist’, the ‘bark dress’, the ‘antelope’, the ‘meat hook’, the ‘coins’, the ‘caustic pickle’, the ‘twisting bar’, the ‘straw mat’; being splashed with hot oil, being fed to the dogs, being impaled alive, and being beheaded. ",

  "an2.1:3.2": "‘If I were to commit the kinds of bad deeds for which the kings arrested that bandit, that criminal, ",

  "an2.1:3.6": "Afraid of the fault apparent in the present life, they do not steal the belongings of others. ",
  "an2.1:3.7": "This is called the fault apparent in the present life. ",
  "an2.1:4.1": "What is the fault to do with lives to come? ",
  "an2.1:4.2": "It’s when someone reflects: ",
  "an2.1:4.3": "‘Bad conduct of body, speech, or mind has a bad, painful result in the next life. ",

  "an2.1:4.6": "Afraid of the fault to do with lives to come, they give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure. ",
  "an2.1:4.7": "This is called the fault to do with lives to come. ",
  "an2.1:4.8": "These are the two faults. ",
  "an2.1:4.9": "So you should train like this: ",
  "an2.1:4.10": "‘We will fear the fault apparent in the present life, and we will fear the fault to do with lives to come. We will fear faults, seeing the danger in faults.’ ",

  "an3.15:3.3": "Then he rolled forth the wheel that had been finished in six days less than six months. ",

  "an4.157:1.3": "Mental and physical. ",
  "an4.157:1.4": "Some sentient beings are seen who can claim to be free of physical illness for a year, or two, or three years … even up to a hundred years or more. ",
  "an4.157:1.5": "But it’s very hard to find any sentient beings in the world who can claim to be free of mental illness even for a moment, apart from those who have ended the defilements. ",
  "an4.157:2.1": "There are four kinds of illness for those gone forth. ",
  "an4.157:2.2": "What four? ",
  "an4.157:2.3": "To start with, a mendicant has many wishes, is frustrated, and is not content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick. ",
  "an4.157:2.4": "Because of this, they focus their corrupt wishes on being looked up to, and on getting material possessions, honor, and popularity. ",
  "an4.157:2.5": "They try hard, strive, and make an effort to get these things. ",
  "an4.157:2.6": "They have an ulterior motive when they visit families. They have an ulterior motive when they sit down, when they speak on Dhamma, and even when they hold it in when they need to go to the toilet. ",
  "an4.157:2.7": "These are the four kinds of illness for those gone forth. ",
  "an4.157:3.1": "So you should train like this: ",
  "an4.157:3.2": "‘We will not have many wishes or be frustrated. We will be content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick. We won’t focus our corrupt wishes on being looked up to, and on getting material possessions, honor, and popularity. We won’t try hard, strive, and make an effort to get these things. We will endure cold, heat, hunger, and thirst. We will endure the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles. We will endure rude and unwelcome criticism. We will put up with physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.’ ",
  "an4.157:3.3": "That’s how you should train.” "

  "an4.198:2.1": "And how does one person mortify themselves, pursuing the practice of mortifying themselves? ",
  "an4.198:2.2": "It’s when someone goes naked, ignoring conventions. They lick their hands, and don’t come or wait when called. They don’t consent to food brought to them, or food prepared on their behalf, or an invitation for a meal. ",
  "an4.198:2.3": "They don’t receive anything from a pot or bowl; or from someone who keeps sheep, or who has a weapon or a shovel in their home; or where a couple is eating; or where there is a woman who is pregnant, breastfeeding, or who has a man in her home; or where there’s a dog waiting or flies buzzing.   "an4.245:3.3": "They examine with wisdom any teachings I taught them. ",

  "an4.245:5.1": "And how is mindfulness its ruler? ",
  "an4.245:5.2": "Mindfulness is well established in oneself: ‘In this way I’ll fulfill the training dealing with supplementary regulations, or support with wisdom in every situation the training dealing with supplementary regulations I’ve already fulfilled.’ ",

  "an4.246:3.4": "If he sees that any part of his body is disordered or displaced, he is displeased. ",

  "an4.255:2.4": "Someone who is liable to get sick, knowing the drawback in what gets sick, searches for that which is free of sickness, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke, extinguishment. ",
  "an4.255:2.5": "Someone who is liable to die, knowing the drawback in what dies, searches for that which is free of death, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke, extinguishment. ",

  "an6.30:0.1": "Numbered Discourses 6.30 ",
  "an6.30:0.2": "3. Unsurpassable ",
  "an6.30:0.3": "Unsurpassable ",
  "an6.30:1.1": "“Mendicants, these six things are unsurpassable. ",
  "an6.30:1.2": "What six? ",
  "an6.30:1.3": "The unsurpassable seeing, listening, acquisition, training, service, and recollection. ",
  "an6.30:2.1": "And what is the unsurpassable seeing? ",
  "an6.30:2.2": "Some people go to see an elephant-treasure, a horse-treasure, a jewel-treasure, or a diverse spectrum of sights; or ascetics and brahmins of wrong view and wrong practice. ",
  "an6.30:2.3": "There is such a seeing, I don’t deny it. ",
  "an6.30:2.4": "That seeing is low, crude, ordinary, ignoble, and pointless. It doesn’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment. ",
  "an6.30:2.5": "The unsurpassable seeing is when someone with settled faith and love, sure and devoted, goes to see a Realized One or their disciple. This is in order to purify sentient beings, to get past sorrow and crying, to make an end of pain and sadness, to discover the system, and to realize extinguishment. ",
  "an6.30:2.6": "This is called the unsurpassable seeing. ",
  "an6.30:2.7": "Such is the unsurpassable seeing. ",
  "an6.30:3.1": "But what of the unsurpassable hearing? ",
  "an6.30:3.2": "Some people go to hear the sound of drums, arched harps, singing, or a diverse spectrum of sounds; or ascetics and brahmins of wrong view and wrong practice. ",
  "an6.30:3.3": "There is such a hearing, I don’t deny it. ",
  "an6.30:3.4": "That hearing … doesn’t lead to extinguishment. ",
  "an6.30:3.5": "The unsurpassable hearing is when someone with settled faith and love, sure and devoted, goes to hear the teaching of a Realized One or one of his disciples. … ",
  "an6.30:3.6": "This is called the unsurpassable hearing. ",

  "an7.21:5.1": "As long as the Vajjis honor, respect, esteem, and venerate Vajjian elders, and think them worth listening to, ",

When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. These dear beings, however, did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never spoke ill of the noble ones; they had right view; and they acted out of that right view. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, I saw sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. I understood how sentient beings are reborn according to their deeds. ",
  "an8.11:17.1": "This was the second knowledge, which I achieved in the middle watch of the night. ",
  "an8.11:17.2": "Ignorance was destroyed and knowledge arose; darkness was destroyed and light arose, as happens for a meditator who is diligent, keen, and resolute. ",
  "an8.11:17.3": "This was my second breaking out, like a chick breaking out of the eggshell. ",

  "an8.25:2.3": "they’re considered to be an ethical lay follower.” ",
  "an8.25:3.1": "“But how do we define a lay follower who is practicing to benefit themselves, not others?” ",
  "an8.25:3.2": "“A lay follower is accomplished in faith, but doesn’t encourage others to do the same. ",
  "an8.25:3.3": "They’re accomplished in ethical conduct, but don’t encourage others to do the same. ",

  "an8.25:3.7": "They readily memorize the teachings they’ve heard, but don’t encourage others to do the same. ",
  "an8.25:3.8": "They examine the meaning of the teachings they’ve memorized, but don’t encourage others to do the same. ",
  "an8.25:3.9": "Understanding the meaning and the teaching, they practice accordingly, but they don’t encourage others to do the same. ",

  "an8.76:0.2": "8. Pairs ",
  "an8.76:0.3": "Accomplishments (2nd) ",
  "an8.76:1.1": "“Mendicants, there are these eight accomplishments. ",
  "an8.76:1.2": "What eight? ",
  "an8.76:1.3": "Accomplishment in initiative, protection, good friendship, and balanced finances. And accomplishment in faith, ethics, generosity, and wisdom. ",
  "an8.76:1.4": "And what is accomplishment in initiative? ",
  "an8.76:1.5": "It’s when a gentleman earns a living by means such as ",
  "an8.76:1.6": "farming, trade, raising cattle, archery, government service, or one of the professions. ",
  "an8.76:1.7": "He understands how to go about these things in order to complete and organize the work. ",
  "an8.76:1.8": "This is called accomplishment in initiative. ",
  "an8.76:2.1": "And what is accomplishment in protection? ",
  "an8.76:2.2": "It’s when a gentleman owns legitimate wealth that he has earned by his own efforts and initiative, built up with his own hands, gathered by the sweat of the brow. He ensures it is guarded and protected, thinking: ",
  "an8.76:2.3": "‘How can I prevent my wealth from being taken by rulers or bandits, consumed by fire, swept away by flood, or taken by unloved heirs?’ ",
  "an8.76:2.4": "This is called accomplishment in protection. ",
  "an8.76:3.1": "And what is accomplishment in good friendship? ",
  "an8.76:3.2": "It’s when a gentleman resides in a town or village. And in that place there are householders or their children who may be young or old, but are mature in conduct, accomplished in faith, ethics, generosity, and wisdom. He associates with them, converses and engages in discussion. And he emulates the same kind of accomplishment in faith, ethics, generosity, and wisdom. ",
  "an8.76:3.3": "This is called accomplishment in good friendship. ",
  "an8.76:4.1": "And what is accomplishment in balanced finances? ",
  "an8.76:4.2": "It’s when a gentleman, knowing his income and expenditure, balances his finances, being neither too extravagant nor too frugal. He thinks, ‘In this way my income will exceed my expenditure, not the reverse.’ ",
  "an8.76:4.3": "It’s like an appraiser or their apprentice who, holding up the scales, knows that it’s low by this much or high by this much. ",
  "an8.76:4.4": "In the same way, a gentleman, knowing his income and expenditure, balances his finances, being neither too extravagant nor too frugal. He thinks, ‘In this way my income will exceed my expenditure, not the reverse.’ ",
  "an8.76:4.5": "If a gentleman has little income but an opulent life, people will say: ‘This gentleman eats their wealth like a fig-eater!’ ",
  "an8.76:4.6": "If a gentleman has a large income but a spartan life, people will say: ‘This gentleman is starving themselves to death!’ ",
  "an8.76:4.7": "But a gentleman, knowing his income and expenditure, leads a balanced life, neither too extravagant nor too frugal, thinking, ‘In this way my income will exceed my expenditure, not the reverse.’ ",
  "an8.76:4.8": "This is called accomplishment in balanced finances. ",
  "an8.76:5.1": "And what is accomplishment in faith? ",
  "an8.76:5.2": "It’s when a gentleman has faith in the Realized One’s awakening: ",
  "an8.76:5.3": "‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha … teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’ ",
  "an8.76:5.4": "This is called accomplishment in faith. ",
  "an8.76:6.1": "And what is accomplishment in ethics? ",
  "an8.76:6.2": "It’s when a gentleman doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume alcoholic drinks that cause negligence. ",
  "an8.76:6.3": "This is called accomplishment in ethics. ",
  "an8.76:7.1": "And what is accomplishment in generosity? ",
  "an8.76:7.2": "It’s when a gentleman lives at home rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share. ",
  "an8.76:7.3": "This is called accomplishment in generosity. ",
  "an8.76:8.1": "And what is accomplishment in wisdom? ",
  "an8.76:8.2": "It’s when a gentleman is wise. He has the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering. ",
  "an8.76:8.3": "This is called accomplishment in wisdom. ",
  "an8.76:9.1": "These are the eight accomplishments. ",
  "an8.76:10.1": "They’re enterprising in the workplace, ",
  "an8.76:10.2": "diligent in managing things, ",
  "an8.76:10.3": "they balance their finances, ",
  "an8.76:10.4": "and preserve their wealth. ",
  "an8.76:11.1": "Faithful, accomplished in ethics, ",
  "an8.76:11.2": "bountiful, rid of stinginess, ",
  "an8.76:11.3": "they always purify the path ",
  "an8.76:11.4": "to well-being in lives to come. ",
  "an8.76:12.1": "And so these eight qualities ",
  "an8.76:12.2": "of a faithful householder ",
  "an8.76:12.3": "are declared by the one who is truly named ",
  "an8.76:12.4": "to lead to happiness in both spheres, ",
  "an8.76:13.1": "welfare and benefit in this life, ",
  "an8.76:13.2": "and happiness in the next. ",
  "an8.76:13.3": "This is how, for a householder, ",
  "an8.76:13.4": "merit grows by generosity.” "

They spoke ill of the noble ones; they had wrong view; and they acted out of that wrong view. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. These dear beings, however, did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never spoke ill of the noble ones; they had right view; and they acted out of that right view. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, he sees sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place.   "an10.51:0.2": "6. Your Own Mind ",
  "an10.51:0.3": "Your Own Mind ",
  "an10.51:1.1": "At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. ",
  "an10.51:1.2": "There the Buddha addressed the mendicants, ",
  "an10.51:1.3": "“Mendicants!” ",
  "an10.51:1.4": "“Venerable sir,” they replied. ",
  "an10.51:1.5": "The Buddha said this: ",
  "an10.51:2.1": "“Mendicants, if a mendicant isn’t skilled in the ways of another’s mind, then they should train themselves: ‘I will be skilled in the ways of my own mind.’ ",
  "an10.51:2.2": "",
  "an10.51:3.1": "And how is a mendicant skilled in the ways of their own mind? ",
  "an10.51:3.2": "Suppose there was a woman or man who was young, youthful, and fond of adornments, and they check their own reflection in a clean bright mirror or a clear bowl of water. If they see any dirt or blemish there, they’d try to remove it. ",
  "an10.51:3.3": "But if they don’t see any dirt or blemish there, they’re happy with that, as they’ve got all they wished for: ",
  "an10.51:3.4": "‘How fortunate that I’m clean!’ ",
  "an10.51:3.5": "In the same way, checking is very helpful for a mendicant’s skillful qualities. ",
  "an10.51:3.6": "‘Am I often covetous or not? Am I often malicious or not? Am I often overcome with dullness and drowsiness or not? Am I often restless or not? Am I often doubtful or not? Am I often irritable or not? Am I often corrupted in mind or not? Am I often disturbed in body or not? Am I often energetic or not? Am I often immersed in samādhi or not?’ ",
  "an10.51:4.1": "Suppose that, upon checking, a mendicant knows this: ",
  "an10.51:4.2": "‘I am often covetous, malicious, overcome with dullness and drowsiness, restless, doubtful, irritable, defiled in mind, disturbed in body, lazy, and not immersed in samādhi.’ In order to give up those bad, unskillful qualities, they should apply intense enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness. ",
  "an10.51:4.3": "Suppose your clothes or head were on fire. In order to extinguish it, you’d apply intense enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness. ",
  "an10.51:4.4": "In the same way, in order to give up those bad, unskillful qualities, that mendicant should apply intense enthusiasm … ",
  "an10.51:5.1": "But suppose that, upon checking, a mendicant knows this: ",
  "an10.51:5.2": "‘I am often content, kind-hearted, free of dullness and drowsiness, calm, confident, loving, pure in mind, undisturbed in body, energetic, and immersed in samādhi.’ Grounded on those skillful qualities, they should practice meditation further to end the defilements.” "

  "an10.60:4.4": "And so they meditate observing impermanence in the five grasping aggregates. ",

  "an10.60:5.1": "And what is the perception of not-self? ",

  "an10.60:5.3": "‘The eye and sights, ear and sounds, nose and smells, tongue and tastes, body and touches, and mind and ideas are not-self.’ ",
  "an10.60:5.4": "And so they meditate observing not-self in the six interior and exterior sense fields. ",
  "an10.60:5.5": "This is called the perception of not-self. ",
  "an10.60:6.1": "And what is the perception of ugliness? ",
  "an10.60:6.2": "It’s when a mendicant examines their own body up from the soles of the feet and down from the tips of the hairs, wrapped in skin and full of many kinds of filth. ",
  "an10.60:6.3": "‘In this body there is head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, diaphragm, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, undigested food, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, urine.’ ",
  "an10.60:6.4": "And so they meditate observing ugliness in this body. ",
  "an10.60:6.5": "This is called the perception of ugliness. ",

  "an10.60:7.3": "‘This body has much suffering and many drawbacks. For this body is beset with many kinds of affliction, such as the following. ",

  "an11.1:1.4": "“Sir, what is the purpose and benefit of skillful ethics?” ",

  "an11.1:2.1": "“But what is the purpose and benefit of having no regrets?” ",
  "an11.1:2.2": "“Joy is the purpose and benefit of having no regrets.” ",
  "an11.1:3.1": "“But what is the purpose and benefit of joy?” ",
  "an11.1:3.2": "“Rapture …” ",
  "an11.1:4.1": "“But what is the purpose and benefit of rapture?” ",
  "an11.1:4.2": "“Tranquility …” ",
  "an11.1:5.1": "“But what is the purpose and benefit of tranquility?” ",
  "an11.1:5.2": "“Bliss …” ",
  "an11.1:6.1": "“But what is the purpose and benefit of bliss?” ",
  "an11.1:6.2": "“Immersion …” ",
  "an11.1:7.1": "“But what is the purpose and benefit of immersion?” ",
  "an11.1:7.2": "“Truly knowing and seeing …” ",
  "an11.1:8.1": "“But what is the purpose and benefit of truly knowing and seeing?” ",
  "an11.1:8.2": "“Disillusionment …” ",
  "an11.1:9.1": "“But what is the purpose and benefit of disillusionment?” ",
  "an11.1:9.2": "“Dispassion …” ",
  "an11.1:10.1": "“But what is the purpose and benefit of dispassion?” ",
  "an11.1:10.2": "“Knowledge and vision of freedom is the purpose and benefit of dispassion. ",
  "an11.1:11.1": "So, Ānanda, the purpose and benefit of skillful ethics is not having regrets. ",

  "an11.1:11.3": "Rapture is the purpose and benefit of joy. ",
  "an11.1:11.4": "Tranquility is the purpose and benefit of rapture. ",
  "an11.1:11.5": "Bliss is the purpose and benefit of tranquility. ",

  "an11.1:11.9": "Dispassion is the purpose and benefit of disillusionment. ",
  "an11.1:11.10": "And knowledge and vision of freedom is the purpose and benefit of dispassion. ",
  "an11.1:11.11": "So, Ānanda, skillful ethics progressively lead up to the highest.” "

  "an11.2:0.1": "Numbered Discourses 11.2 ",
  "an11.2:0.2": "1. Dependence ",
  "an11.2:0.3": "Making a Wish ",
  "an11.2:1.1": "“Mendicants, an ethical person, who has fulfilled ethical conduct, need not make a wish: ",
  "an11.2:1.2": "‘May I have no regrets!’ ",
  "an11.2:1.3": "It’s only natural that an ethical person has no regrets. ",
  "an11.2:2.1": "When you have no regrets you need not make a wish: ",
  "an11.2:2.2": "‘May I feel joy!’ ",
  "an11.2:2.3": "It’s only natural that joy springs up when you have no regrets. ",
  "an11.2:3.1": "When you feel joy you need not make a wish: ",
  "an11.2:3.2": "‘May I experience rapture!’ ",
  "an11.2:3.3": "It’s only natural that rapture arises when you’re joyful. ",
  "an11.2:4.1": "When your mind is full of rapture you need not make a wish: ",
  "an11.2:4.2": "‘May my body become tranquil!’ ",
  "an11.2:4.3": "It’s only natural that your body becomes tranquil when your mind is full of rapture. ",
  "an11.2:5.1": "When your body is tranquil you need not make a wish: ",
  "an11.2:5.2": "‘May I feel bliss!’ ",
  "an11.2:5.3": "It’s only natural to feel bliss when your body is tranquil. ",
  "an11.2:6.1": "When you feel bliss you need not make a wish: ",
  "an11.2:6.2": "‘May my mind be immersed in samādhi!’ ",
  "an11.2:6.3": "It’s only natural for the mind to become immersed in samādhi when you feel bliss. ",
  "an11.2:7.1": "When your mind is immersed in samādhi you need not make a wish: ",
  "an11.2:7.2": "‘May I truly know and see!’ ",
  "an11.2:7.3": "It’s only natural to truly know and see when your mind is immersed in samādhi. ",
  "an11.2:8.1": "When you truly know and see you need not make a wish: ",
  "an11.2:8.2": "‘May I grow disillusioned!’ ",
  "an11.2:8.3": "It’s only natural to grow disillusioned when you truly know and see. ",
  "an11.2:9.1": "When you’re disillusioned you need not make a wish: ",
  "an11.2:9.2": "‘May I become dispassionate!’ ",
  "an11.2:9.3": "It’s only natural to grow dispassionate when you’re disillusioned. ",
  "an11.2:10.1": "When you’re dispassionate you need not make a wish: ",
  "an11.2:10.2": "‘May I realize the knowledge and vision of freedom!’ ",
  "an11.2:10.3": "It’s only natural to realize the knowledge and vision of freedom when you’re dispassionate. ",
  "an11.2:11.1": "And so, mendicants, the knowledge and vision of freedom is the purpose and benefit of dispassion. Dispassion is the purpose and benefit of disillusionment. Disillusionment is the purpose and benefit of truly knowing and seeing. Truly knowing and seeing is the purpose and benefit of immersion. Immersion is the purpose and benefit of bliss. Bliss is the purpose and benefit of tranquility. Tranquility is the purpose and benefit of rapture. Rapture is the purpose and benefit of joy. Joy is the purpose and benefit of not having regrets. Not having regrets is the purpose and benefit of skillful ethics. ",
  "an11.2:11.2": "And so, mendicants, good qualities flow on and fill up from one to the other, for going from the near shore to the far shore.” "

  "an11.3:0.2": "1. Dependence ",
  "an11.3:0.3": "Vital Conditions (1st) ",
  "an11.3:1.1": "“Mendicants, an unethical person, who lacks ethics, has destroyed a vital condition for having no regrets. ",
  "an11.3:1.2": "When there are regrets, one who has regrets has destroyed a vital condition for joy. ",
  "an11.3:1.3": "When there is no joy, one who lacks joy has destroyed a vital condition for rapture. ",
  "an11.3:1.4": "When there is no rapture, one who lacks rapture has destroyed a vital condition for tranquility. ",
  "an11.3:1.5": "When there is no tranquility, one who lacks tranquility has destroyed a vital condition for bliss. ",
  "an11.3:1.6": "When there is no bliss, one who lacks bliss has destroyed a vital condition for right immersion. ",
  "an11.3:1.7": "When there is no right immersion, one who lacks right immersion has destroyed a vital condition for true knowledge and vision. ",
  "an11.3:1.8": "When there is no true knowledge and vision, one who lacks true knowledge and vision has destroyed a vital condition for disillusionment. ",
  "an11.3:1.9": "When there is no disillusionment, one who lacks disillusionment has destroyed a vital condition for dispassion. ",
  "an11.3:1.10": "When there is no dispassion, one who lacks dispassion has destroyed a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom. ",
  "an11.3:2.1": "Suppose there was a tree that lacked branches and foliage. Its shoots, bark, softwood, and heartwood would not grow to fullness. ",
  "an11.3:2.2": "In the same way, an unethical person, who lacks ethics, has destroyed a vital condition for having no regrets. ",
  "an11.3:2.3": "When there are regrets, one who has regrets has destroyed a vital condition for joy. … ",
  "an11.3:2.4": "When there is no dispassion, one who lacks dispassion has destroyed a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom. ",
  "an11.3:3.1": "An ethical person, who has fulfilled ethics, has fulfilled a vital condition for not having regrets. ",
  "an11.3:3.2": "When there are no regrets, one who has no regrets has fulfilled a vital condition for joy. ",
  "an11.3:3.3": "When there is joy, one who has fulfilled joy has fulfilled a vital condition for rapture. ",
  "an11.3:3.4": "When there is rapture, one who has fulfilled rapture has fulfilled a vital condition for tranquility. ",
  "an11.3:3.5": "When there is tranquility, one who has fulfilled tranquility has fulfilled a vital condition for bliss. ",
  "an11.3:3.6": "When there is bliss, one who has fulfilled bliss has fulfilled a vital condition for right immersion. ",
  "an11.3:3.7": "When there is right immersion, one who has fulfilled right immersion has fulfilled a vital condition for true knowledge and vision. ",
  "an11.3:3.8": "When there is true knowledge and vision, one who has fulfilled true knowledge and vision has fulfilled a vital condition for disillusionment. ",
  "an11.3:3.9": "When there is disillusionment, one who has fulfilled disillusionment has fulfilled a vital condition for dispassion. ",
  "an11.3:3.10": "When there is dispassion, one who has fulfilled dispassion has fulfilled a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom. ",

  "an11.3:4.3": "When there are no regrets, one who has no regrets has fulfilled a vital condition for joy. … ",
  "an11.3:4.4": "When there is dispassion, one who has fulfilled dispassion has fulfilled a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.” "

  "an11.6:0.3": "Disasters ",
  "an11.6:1.1": "“Mendicants, any mendicant who abuses and insults their spiritual companions, speaking ill of the noble ones, will, without a doubt, fall into one or other of these eleven disasters. ",
  "an11.6:2.1": "What eleven? ",
  "an11.6:2.2": "They don’t achieve the unachieved. ",
  "an11.6:2.3": "What they have achieved falls away. ",

  "dn22:2.0.1": "1. Observing the Body ",
  "dn22:2.0.2": "1.1. Mindfulness of Breathing ",
  "dn22:2.1": "And how does a mendicant meditate observing an aspect of the body? ",
  "dn22:2.2": "It’s when a mendicant—gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut—sits down cross-legged, sets their body straight, and establishes mindfulness in front of them. ",
  "dn22:2.3": "Just mindful, they breathe in. Mindful, they breathe out. ",
  "dn22:2.4": "Breathing in heavily they know: ‘I’m breathing in heavily.’ Breathing out heavily they know: ‘I’m breathing out heavily.’ ",
  "dn22:2.5": "When breathing in lightly they know: ‘I’m breathing in lightly.’ Breathing out lightly they know: ‘I’m breathing out lightly.’ ",

  "dn28:17.0": "1.14. Death and Rebirth ",
  "dn28:17.1": "And moreover, sir, how the Buddha teaches the knowledge of the death and rebirth of sentient beings is unsurpassable. ",
  "dn28:17.2": "It’s when some ascetic or brahmin—by dint of keen, resolute, committed, and diligent effort, and right application of mind—experiences an immersion of the heart of such a kind that with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn— ",
  "dn28:17.3": "inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings are reborn according to their deeds: ‘These dear beings did bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. They spoke ill of the noble ones; they had wrong view; and they chose to act out of that wrong view. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. These dear beings, however, did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never spoke ill of the noble ones; they had right view; and they chose to act out of that right view. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings are reborn according to their deeds. ",

  "dn31:27.0": "13. Covering the Six Directions ",
  "dn31:27.1": "“And how, householder’s son, does a noble disciple cover the six directions? ",
  "dn31:27.2": "These six directions should be recognized: ",
  "dn31:27.3": "parents as the east, teachers as the south, partner and children as the west, friends and colleagues as the north, bondservants and workers as beneath, and ascetics and brahmins as above. ",
  "dn31:28.1": "A child should serve their parents as the eastern quarter in five ways, thinking: ",
  "dn31:28.2": "‘I will support those who supported me. I’ll do my duty for them. I’ll maintain the family lineage. I’ll take care of the inheritance. When they have passed away, I’ll make an offering on their behalf.’ ",
  "dn31:28.3": "Parents served by the children in these five ways show compassion to them in five ways. ",
  "dn31:28.4": "They keep them from doing bad. They support them in doing good. They train them in a profession. They connect them with a suitable partner. They transfer the inheritance in due time. ",
  "dn31:28.5": "Parents served by their children in these five ways show compassion to them in these five ways. ",
  "dn31:28.6": "And that’s how the eastern quarter is covered, kept safe and free of peril. ",
  "dn31:29.1": "A student should serve their teacher as the southern quarter in five ways: ",
  "dn31:29.2": "by rising for them, by serving them, by listening well, by looking after them, and by carefully learning their profession. ",
  "dn31:29.3": "Teachers served by their students in these five ways show compassion to them in five ways. ",
  "dn31:29.4": "They make sure they’re well educated and well drilled in memorization. They clearly explain all the knowledge of the profession. They introduce them to their friends and colleagues. They provide protection in every region. ",
  "dn31:29.5": "Teachers served by their students in these five ways show compassion to them in these five ways. ",
  "dn31:29.6": "And that’s how the southern quarter is covered, kept safe and free of peril. ",
  "dn31:30.1": "A husband should serve his wife as the western quarter in five ways: ",
  "dn31:30.2": "by treating her with honor, by not looking down on her, by not being unfaithful, by relinquishing authority to her, and by presenting her with adornments. ",
  "dn31:30.3": "A wife served by her husband in these five ways shows compassion to him in five ways. ",
  "dn31:30.4": "She’s well-organized in her work. She manages the domestic help. She’s not unfaithful. She preserves his earnings. She’s deft and tireless in all her duties. ",

  "iti99:0.1": "So It Was Said 99 ",
  "iti99:0.2": "The Book of the Threes ",
  "iti99:0.3": "Chapter Five ",
  "iti99:0.4": "The Three Knowledges ",
  "iti99:1.1": "This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard. ",
  "iti99:2.1": "“Mendicants, I describe a brahmin who is master of the three Vedic knowledges in terms of the teaching, not by mere oral recitation. ",
  "iti99:3.1": "How so? ",
  "iti99:3.2": "It’s when a mendicant recollects many kinds of past lives. That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. They remember: ‘There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.’ And so they recollect their many kinds of past lives, with features and details. ",
  "iti99:3.3": "This is the first knowledge they achieved. Ignorance was destroyed and knowledge arose; darkness was destroyed and light arose, as happens for a meditator who is diligent, keen, and resolute. ",
  "iti99:4.1": "Furthermore, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, a mendicant sees sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings are reborn according to their deeds: ‘These dear beings did bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. They spoke ill of the noble ones; they had wrong view; and they chose to act out of that wrong view. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. These dear beings, however, did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never spoke ill of the noble ones; they had right view; and they chose to act out of that right view. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings are reborn according to their deeds. ",
  "iti99:4.2": "This is the second knowledge they achieved. Ignorance was destroyed and knowledge arose; darkness was destroyed and light arose, as happens for a meditator who is diligent, keen, and resolute. ",

When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place.   "sn45.8:6.1": "And what is right action? ",
  "sn45.8:6.2": "Avoiding killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual activity. ",
  "sn45.8:6.3": "This is called right action. ",
  "sn45.8:7.1": "And what is right livelihood? ",
  "sn45.8:7.2": "It’s when a noble disciple gives up wrong livelihood and earns a living by right livelihood. ",
  "sn45.8:7.3": "This is called right livelihood. ",
  "sn45.8:8.1": "And what is right effort? ",
  "sn45.8:8.2": "It’s when a mendicant generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise. ",
  "sn45.8:8.3": "They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen are given up. ",
  "sn45.8:8.4": "They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have not arisen do arise. ",
  "sn45.8:8.5": "They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fulfilled by development. ",
  "sn45.8:8.6": "This is called right effort. ",
  "sn45.8:9.1": "And what is right mindfulness? ",

  "sn45.8:9.3": "They meditate observing an aspect of feelings—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world. ",

  "sn45.8:9.5": "They meditate observing an aspect of principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world. ",
  "sn45.8:9.6": "This is called right mindfulness. ",
